artists.biography:
Jean Michel André Jarre (born 24 August 1948 in Lyon) is a French composer, performer and music producer. He is a pioneer in the electronic, ambient and New Age genres, and known as an organiser of outdoor spectacles of his music featuring lights, laser displays, and fireworks.

Jarre was raised in Lyon by his mother and grandparents, and trained on the piano. From an early age he was introduced to a variety of art forms, including those of street performers, jazz musicians, and the artist Pierre Soulages. He played guitar in a band, but his musical style was perhaps most heavily influenced by Pierre Schaeffer, a pioneer of musique concrète at the Groupe de Recherches Musicales.

His first mainstream success was the 1976 album Oxygène. Recorded in a makeshift studio at his home, the album sold an estimated 12 million copies. Oxygène was followed in 1978 by Équinoxe, and in 1979 Jarre performed to a record-breaking audience of more than a million people at the Place de la Concorde, a record he has since broken three times. More albums were to follow, but his 1979 concert served as a blueprint for his future performances around the world. Several of his albums have been released to coincide with large-scale outdoor events, and he is now perhaps as well known as a performer as a musician.

As of 2004 Jarre had sold an estimated 80 million albums. He was the first Western musician to be allowed to perform in the People's Republic of China, and holds the world record for the largest-ever audience at an outdoor event.

perplexity.description:
Oxymore is Jean-Michel Jarre's 22nd studio album, released in October 2024 via Sony Music. Conceived as an immersive work in multi-channel and 3D binaural sound, the album represents one of Jarre's most ambitious projects to date, pushing the boundaries of how electronic music is composed, mixed, and produced. The album was recorded and mixed in audio 360 at Radio France's "Innovation" studios, making it the first commercial release of this scale to fully utilize multichannel and binaural spatial audio technology.

The album draws inspiration from the French movement musique concrète, a compositional approach developed in the 1940s that uses recorded sounds as raw material. Jarre reinvents this foundational electronic music concept using contemporary production tools, creating a musical journey that blends analogue and digital soundscapes. Oxymore serves as a tribute to the late French composer Pierre Henry, a pioneer of musique concrète and a significant influence on Jarre's early work at the Groupe de Recherche Musicales. Henry's widow provided stems of material originally intended for a collaboration with Jarre, which are woven throughout the album.

The project extends beyond audio, accompanied by a groundbreaking VR universe called "Oxyville" designed to enhance the listening experience. Tracks such as "Oxymore," "Sonic Land," and "Brutalism" showcase complex, atmospheric compositions that build into dynamic rhythmic passages, while other pieces like "Neon Lips" and "Synthy Sisters" demonstrate a more playful yet conceptually rigorous approach. The album is available in multiple formats including CD, double vinyl, and digital versions in stereo, binaural, 5.1, and Dolby Atmos, with physical copies including access codes to the highest-quality binaural master as intended by Jarre.
